Hey all! Despite our relative silence we've continued to work hard on http://pcmratings.com/, and the site is now online! As I'm sure you've all noticed, several other sites making use of the rating system have already launched. We've taken their launch as a good sign of the interest in exploring this, and we've been watching the feedback for those sites to try and figure out how we can best put ours together to service the community.

Some specific things we decided:

  1. Ratings are controlled by moderators with community input. We saw aggregate ratings not turn out as effective as we had all hoped, so we decided this was the best option. We've got a system for submitting the information for the moderators to use to generate ratings, as well as to contest the current rating.
  2. Users are allowed to submit their own text-only reviews, with a manually selected PCMRG rating. They don't automatically influence the "official" rating, but the information in them may be used by mods to adjust the rating. We don't expect users to remain objective with their review/rating, we're encouraging users to use the space to voice their concerns/love for a particular game freely. We're working on an up/down vote mechanism for the user reviews so that the most helpful reviews will be at the top and trolling reviews will naturally fade to the bottom.
  3. It uses REddit as an authentication mechanism (we're looking into adding Voat support). As a basic troll-prevention mechanism, we're requiring a minimum comment karma of 100 in order to log in.
  4. We've moved away from the "select 1 option from each category" system to a system based on scoring independent options. They are still categorized for organizational purposes. The latest details of the rating system should always be visible at http://pcmratings.com/about.php

We're open to feedback on just about all aspects of the site, and we'll probably be looking to bring on some extra moderators to help set up ratings if the work load is too much for our current crew. There is still need for visual polish on some pages, it will be coming in the near future.

EDIT: Changed to reflect the site being launched.

What is perfect competition and how does it relate to free markets?

Perfect competition is an economic model that describes a hypothetical kind of market.

Everyone in a perfectly competitive market is a price taker. There is a large number of buyers and sellers, and no agent in the market has any "market power" to influence the market price.

There are no barriers to entering a perfectly competitive market, it is extremely easy for firms to join and leave such a market.

The products sold are completely homogenous. The product sold by Firm A is identical to the one sold by Firms B, C, D and so on.

In a perfectly competitive market, there are so many firms that each firm will charge a price equal to their marginal revenue (everyone will break exactly even.) Profit does not exist in a perfectly competitive market.

Strict perfect competition does not exist in the real world as it would require infinite buyers, infinite sellers, and a bunch of other extreme conditions. But markets that resemble perfect competition exist: agriculture being the most common example. Let's take corn. There are a ton of farmers and they all produce identical corn. Corn has a clear-cut "market price" and thus an individual farmer has no market power to charge another price. If he charges even a cent more than the market price then no one will buy from him.

Free markets do not naturally equilibrate at perfect competition. Markets with high barriers to entry (oil, diamonds, pharmaceuticals) naturally don't have many sellers and therefore there is room for firms to make decisions about price.

And in the real world, most products are not homogenous. There are brands with different formulas, variations, mechanisms, etc. and patents help make this the case.

Monopolistic competition is probably the sort of competition you encounter most. It's imperfect competition, you have multiple finite choices that are different from one another.

Oligopoly sits farther down the spectrum where there are a very small number of firms with tremendous market power. Think Coca-Cola and Pepsi.

And Monopoly is what it is: there is one firm in the market that will freely set its price without having to consider other firms.
